msy-al-reyada-girls-centre.about:
Al Reyada Girls Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 5-39, with a focus on social, cultural and sports skills for girls.

Founded in 2016, it aims to empower girls in social, cultural and sports fields by giving them a supportive environment to develop their talents and learn new skills. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
A local place to build skills and friendships
msy-al-reyada-girls-centre.eligibility: Young people aged 5-39 living in Qatar. Activities are mostly in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open the centre's page on the Ministry of Sports and Youth website
Contact the centre (Alreyada@msy.gov.qa) or visit during opening hours
Register as a member or for a specific activity
msy-al-reyada-girls-centre.costs: Most activities are free or low-cost.

msy-al-wakra-girls-centre.about:
Al Wakra Girls Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 14-39, with a focus on skills, culture and community activities for young women.

Founded in 2016 in Al Wakra, south of Doha, it serves young women in the area with workshops, courses and community events. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
A local place to build skills and friendships
msy-al-wakra-girls-centre.eligibility: Young people aged 14-39 living in Qatar. Activities are mostly in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open the centre's page on the Ministry of Sports and Youth website
Contact the centre (alwakragirls@msy.gov.qa) or visit during opening hours
Register as a member or for a specific activity

msy-barzan-youth-centre.about:
Barzan Youth Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 10-30, with a focus on cultural, skills and values programmes for boys and young men.

Founded in 1994, it develops young Qataris culturally and in practical skills, and strengthens national belonging through targeted programmes. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.

A local place to build skills and friendships

msy-doha-girls-centre.about:
Doha Girls Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 15-39, with a focus on empowering young women through cultural, social and skills programmes.

Founded in 2012, it is a women-only centre that aims to be a leading model for empowering young women locally and internationally. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.

A local place to build skills and friendships

msy-doha-youth-centre.about:
Doha Youth Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 15-39, with a focus on leadership, painting and sculpture, photography, camping and trips.

Founded in 1983, it is one of Qatar's oldest youth centres and aims to build confident young leaders through cultural, social and educational programmes for both young men and women. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
A local place to build skills and friendships

msy-friends-of-environment-centre.about:
Friends of the Environment Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 15-39, with a focus on environmental awareness, sustainability and volunteering.

Founded in 1992, it specialises in raising environmental awareness among the public and young people in Qatar, with campaigns, field activities and volunteering for sustainable development. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
A local place to build skills and friendships

msy-saif-al-ghariya-youth-centre.about:
Saif Al Ghariya Youth Centre is one of the youth centres run under Qatar's Ministry of Sports and Youth. It offers year-round free or low-cost activities, workshops, trips and clubs for young people aged 15-39, with a focus on marine sports, sea fishing, teamwork and community responsibility.

Founded in 2021, it aims to empower young people and encourage teamwork, dialogue and positive community participation through quality programmes and partnerships. Activities are announced on the centre's channels and on the Ministry's youth events calendar, and most are in Arabic. Young people can drop in, join as members or sign up for individual workshops and trips.
highlights: Free or low-cost activities run by the Ministry of Sports and Youth
A local place to build skills and friendships
msy-saif-al-ghariya-youth-centre.eligibility: Young people aged 15-39 living in Qatar. Activities are mostly in Arabic.

Register as a member or for a specific activity

msy-youth-initiatives-incubator.about:
The Youth Initiatives Incubator is a strategic platform of the Ministry of Sports and Youth to discover and support youth initiatives with social and development impact and turn them from ideas into sustainable, scalable projects aligned with Qatar's National Youth Policy. Accepted initiatives go through four stages: selection, capacity-building (initiative design, strategic planning, team management, impact measurement), incubation with mentoring, technical and logistical support and partner links, and graduation.

It targets young people aged 14-35, non-profit youth teams, emerging community initiatives and young social leaders. Focus areas include social issues, youth health, environment, learning, research and innovation, employment and entrepreneurship, humanitarian work and digital media. Applications are made through the online form on the Ministry's page, with an initiative profile, operating plan and proposed budget.
highlights: Seven focus areas from environment to digital media
Accepts ideas as well as running initiatives
msy-youth-initiatives-incubator.eligibility: Young people aged 14-35 in Qatar (the form asks for a Qatari ID number), youth non-profit teams and emerging community initiatives.
how_to_apply: Read the incubator page
Prepare an initiative profile, operating plan and proposed budget
Upload team IDs and CVs in the online registration form
Submit and wait for evaluation
msy-youth-initiatives-incubator.costs: Free; selected initiatives receive in-kind support.

oman-cultural-scientific-cooperation-sch.about:
The Omani Programme for Cultural and Scientific Cooperation with Friendly and Brotherly Countries is managed by MoHERI's Scholarships Section, which also handles scholarships offered to Oman by other countries. Its aim is to build international cooperation and human capacity in priority countries and to attract international students to Oman.

The programme offers a number of scholarships and study missions for first-degree (bachelor's) study at government and private higher education institutions inside Oman. Places are allocated per country, so candidates usually apply through their own education ministry or the Omani embassy.
highlights: Bachelor's study in Oman for international students
oman-cultural-scientific-cooperation-sch.eligibility: Citizens of countries designated by Oman as priority/friendly countries (check with MoHERI or the Omani embassy); secondary-school graduates meeting university admission rules.
how_to_apply: Ask your country's education ministry or the Omani embassy whether seats are offered this year.
Contact MoHERI's postgraduate & scholarships department (postgraduate@moheri.gov.om).
Submit the nomination file (certificates, passport, medical) as instructed.
Await placement at an Omani university.
oman-cultural-scientific-cooperation-sch.costs: Scholarship for undergraduate study in Oman; benefits are set per agreement and institution.

oman-government-external-scholarships-om.about:
MoHERI's External Scholarships (al-bi'that al-kharijiya) fund Omani students for bachelor's study at universities on the ministry's list of recommended foreign universities. Students register for external scholarships through the Higher Education Admission Centre's unified system, competing on their General Education Diploma results and the programme's requirements.

MoHERI publishes the registration mechanism, country guides (including countries supervised by the cultural attaché in Washington), visa and immigration information, and the rules and amounts of financial allocations for scholarship students abroad.
highlights: Full government scholarship to recommended universities abroad
Monthly allocations and support from Omani cultural attachés
oman-government-external-scholarships-om.eligibility: Omani nationals completing the General Education Diploma who meet the grade and programme requirements set in the HEAC student guide.
how_to_apply: Read the HEAC student guide for the year and the list of recommended foreign universities on moheri.gov.om.
Register for external scholarship programmes in the HEAC system during the registration period.
Accept your offer and follow MoHERI's procedure for opening a scholarship file.
Obtain admission and visa with guidance from the cultural attaché.
oman-government-external-scholarships-om.costs: Tuition and living allocations per MoHERI rules for students on scholarships abroad.

oman-national-postgraduate-programme-202.about:
Following royal directives, Oman continued its National Programme for Postgraduate Studies within the 10th five-year plan, in two phases. It covers an academic track, a medical track and a university-grants track, with the aim of sending Omani talent to the best universities worldwide and strengthening scientific and technical exchange.

MoHERI's Postgraduate and Scholarships Department follows the students and also manages scholarships offered to Oman by other countries and institutions (announced on its 'Scholarship announcements' page, e.g. offers from the EU, IsDB, Hungary, Switzerland, Japan and Korean universities). External postgraduate grants are registered through the unified admission centre and announced in the postgraduate student guide.
highlights: Master's and PhD at top universities worldwide
Also lists foreign-government scholarships offered to Omanis
oman-national-postgraduate-programme-202.eligibility: Omani nationals meeting the postgraduate guide's academic criteria (degree classification, admission to a top-ranked university in a priority field).
how_to_apply: Read MoHERI's postgraduate student guide for the cycle.
Secure admission (or apply) to a recommended top university in a priority field.
Register through the Higher Education Admission Centre during the announced window.
Check MoHERI's 'Scholarship announcements' page for additional foreign-government offers.
oman-national-postgraduate-programme-202.costs: Full funding (tuition, allowances) under MoHERI's rules for postgraduate scholars abroad.

qatar-fintech-hub-pre-acceleration.about:
Qatar FinTech Hub (QFTH), launched in 2020 and powered by Qatar Development Bank, supports fintech innovation under Qatar's National FinTech Strategy. Its Pre-Acceleration programme helps early-stage fintechs validate MVPs, align with regulatory frameworks and build investment readiness; the Acceleration programme supports go-to-market, regional expansion, localisation and regulatory licensing; a FinTech Development Grant is available to Qatar-based fintechs.

Seven waves have graduated more than 100 local and international fintechs, with QAR 39.8M+ in programme funding. Startups with a fintech MVP, including student founders, can apply when the next wave opens.
qatar-fintech-hub-pre-acceleration.eligibility: Early-stage and growth fintech startups, local and international.
how_to_apply: Read the programme details on fintech.qa
Apply when the next wave is announced
Prepare your MVP, team and business plan
qatar-fintech-hub-pre-acceleration.costs: Free to apply; programme support and funding for selected startups.

qatar-museums-internships-spring-2027.about:
Qatar Museums (QM) runs internship tracks across its museums and departments, including the National Museum of Qatar, the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art, 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum, Al Khor Museum, the Exhibitions Department, Tasweer Photo Festival and shared services (finance, HR, procurement, IT). Interns contribute to real projects such as exhibitions, education programmes, collections and operations, with flexible start dates depending on the department.

Most tracks are aimed at university students and recent graduates; several require a bachelor's degree and some ask for a university letter. Applications for Fall 2026 are closed, and QM says Spring 2027 opportunities will be shared in March 2027. Applicants may apply for one internship at a time.
highlights: Placements at world-class museums in Doha
Tracks from curation and education to finance and IT
qatar-museums-internships-spring-2027.eligibility: University students and recent graduates (some tracks require a bachelor's degree). Check each track for residency requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse the internship pages on qm.org.qa
Wait for the Spring 2027 listing in March 2027
Apply for one internship through the online form
Prepare a CV and, if required, a university letter

qatar-national-volunteering-platform.about:
Tatawwa ('volunteer') is the National Volunteering Platform of Qatar, operated by the Ministry of Social Development and Family (MSDF). It brings volunteering opportunities from different organisations into one place so that residents can register, browse and apply for opportunities and keep a record of their volunteering.

For students it is the simplest official way to find recognised volunteering in Qatar; age and residency requirements are set on the portal and by each opportunity (many require participants to be 18+).
qatar-national-volunteering-platform.eligibility: Residents of Qatar; check age limits on the portal (many opportunities 18+).
how_to_apply: Open volunteer.gov.qa
Create an account with your Qatari ID
Browse and apply for opportunities

qatar-university-stem-sponsorship-2027.about:
The STEM Sponsorship Program was created to attract Qatari students into science, technology, engineering and mathematics majors in line with Qatar National Vision 2030. Seats per field are set every year according to national needs.

Covered majors (2026 list): for men, chemistry, mathematics, civil engineering, computer science, environmental sciences, statistics, nursing and biomedical sciences; for women, chemistry, mathematics, physics, computer science, physical therapy, statistics, nursing, biomedical sciences and biology. Medicine and dental medicine are excluded.

Sponsored students must keep a GPA of at least 2.5, pass 12+ credit hours per semester and register continuously until graduation.
highlights: QR 3,000 monthly salary plus free textbooks
Open to Qataris and children/husbands of Qataris and Qatari travel-document holders
No documents needed: apply online after declaring your major
qatar-university-stem-sponsorship-2027.eligibility: Qatari nationals, husbands and children of Qatari women, and holders of Qatari travel documents, with a high-school average of at least 75%, accepted into a covered STEM major at QU, not holding another sponsorship or scholarship.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Qatar University.
Declare a major on the STEM sponsorship list.
Log in to the QU sponsorship application system and follow the user guide (no documents required).
Keep GPA ≥ 2.5 and 12+ credits per semester to retain the sponsorship.
qatar-university-stem-sponsorship-2027.costs: QR 3,000 per month plus exemption from textbook fees (tuition is already free for Qatari students at QU).

qatar-university-talent-sponsorship-2027.about:
The Talent Sponsorship rewards Qatari students who have proven achievements in one of QU's talent fields: scientific research (including arts and sciences), technology and innovation, literature, acting (male), media and athletics. Applications are made with the online admission application.

Applicants need at least 75% in the first semester of grade 12, two letters from recognised entities in their field, a statement of talent and achievements with links to videos or portfolios, and a successful interview (athletes also pass a physical fitness exam). A conditional acceptance is sent within six weeks of the sponsorship deadline.

Sponsored students must keep a GPA of 2.3, take 12+ credits a semester and represent QU in their talent field locally and internationally.
highlights: Sponsorship for talent in research, tech, literature, media, acting or sport
qatar-university-talent-sponsorship-2027.eligibility: Qatari nationals (and eligible children/husbands of Qataris, Qatari travel-document holders) with at least 75% in grade 12 first semester and proven recent achievements in one talent field. Cannot be combined with another sponsorship.
how_to_apply: Apply online to Qatar University for Fall 2027 entry.
On the 'Scholarship Application' page, choose the Talent Sponsorship and upload two recommendation letters.
Upload a talent statement with links to videos/portfolio (Dropbox/OneDrive) showing recent achievements.
Attend the interview (and fitness test for sport).
Receive conditional acceptance within ~6 weeks; submit final documents.
qatar-university-talent-sponsorship-2027.costs: Sponsorship benefits per QU's monthly salary scale for sponsorship programmes (monthly allowance; tuition is free for Qataris at QU).

qatar-youth-hostels-programmes.about:
Qatar Youth Hostels was founded in 1983, joined the Arab Federation of Youth Associations the same year and the International Youth Hostel Federation (Hostelling International) in 1986. It is one of the Ministry of Sports and Youth's youth centres and aims to encourage young people to travel, study abroad, serve the environment and learn independence and teamwork.

It runs city tours around Qatar, youth events and activities, camps and 'knowledge programmes' (workshops and training), and operates a hostel in Doha. Membership gives access to these activities and to Hostelling International benefits abroad.
how_to_apply: Visit hi-qatar.com
Register for membership
Sign up for upcoming events and programmes
qatar-youth-hostels-programmes.costs: Membership fee applies; many events low-cost.

qatardebate-iudc-8.about:
The International Universities Debating Championship (IUDC) is QatarDebate's flagship Arabic debating tournament for university students worldwide, including non-native Arabic speakers. National champions usually qualify through national championships, while teams from countries without one can register directly through QatarDebate's form.

The 8th edition has been postponed until further notice for safety reasons, and QatarDebate says it will publish new dates once finalised; team registration and a call for international adjudicators remain open on the official page. It is one of the biggest international stages for Arabic debate.
highlights: Global Arabic debating championship hosted in Doha
Direct registration for countries without a national round
qatardebate-iudc-8.eligibility: University student teams from any country, debating in Arabic; teams from countries with a national championship qualify through it.
how_to_apply: Read the technical guidelines on the IUDC page
Register your university team through the online form
Watch the page for the confirmed dates
qatardebate-iudc-8.costs: Check the official page; QatarDebate has historically covered major costs for qualified teams.

qatardebate-workshops-training.about:
QatarDebate Center, a member of Qatar Foundation, runs workshops and training sessions aligned with the academic calendar. Sessions develop general skills such as overcoming stage fright, public speaking, research and persuasion, as well as technical debating skills like argumentation, motion analysis and rebuttals, mostly in Arabic and some in English.

Workshops are announced on QatarDebate's events page, and schools, universities or organisations can request a dedicated workshop through the inquiries form. They are a good preparation for the Qatar Schools and Universities Debate Leagues.
highlights: Run by Qatar's national debate centre
qatardebate-workshops-training.eligibility: School students, university students, teachers and professionals in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Check the QatarDebate events page for upcoming workshops
Register for a session, or
Ask your school/university to request a workshop via the inquiries form

qcdc-al-dileela-career-counselling.about:
Al-Dileela ('your career navigator') is QCDC's specialised career counselling programme. Sessions follow five phases: assessing your skills and interests, building a career plan and long-term goals, understanding yourself and the job market, interview skills, and personal branding (CV, cover letter, LinkedIn).

It is open to community members in Qatar, including high school students planning their university major, university students, fresh graduates and job seekers. Sessions are online and booked through Snoonu City on a first-come, first-served basis.
highlights: Qualified counsellors from Qatar Foundation's career centre
qcdc-al-dileela-career-counselling.eligibility: Residents of Qatar: high school students, university students, graduates, job seekers and professionals.
how_to_apply: Open the Al-Dileela page
Book sessions through the Snoonu City link
Attend the online sessions in order
qcdc-al-dileela-career-counselling.costs: Booked through Snoonu City; check the booking page for the current price.

qcdc-career-ambassadors-program.about:
The Career Ambassadors Program aims to build leadership and career-planning skills among young people in Qatar under QCDC's motto 'Your Future in Your Hands'. Each participating school nominates five or six students from grades 10 and 11, who attend a series of QCDC training and development workshops over three months.

Ambassadors then represent QCDC at their schools, organising activities, events and workshops that help other students plan their studies and careers. It is a good leadership credential for students interested in education, counselling or student government.
highlights: Leadership role in your own school
qcdc-career-ambassadors-program.eligibility: Grade 10 and 11 students at schools in Qatar, nominated by their school (5-6 per school). Programme focused on Qatari youth.
how_to_apply: Tell your school career counsellor you are interested
Get nominated by your school
Attend QCDC workshops and run activities at school

qcdc-career-camps.about:
QCDC, founded by Qatar Foundation, organises summer and winter Career Camps to help high school students make informed academic and career decisions. Camps mix career-planning workshops, site visits and job-shadowing at leading organisations in Qatar, and recreational, sports and educational activities that build confidence, communication and teamwork.

The final day of each camp introduces universities in Qatar, with representatives explaining their programmes and admission requirements. Camps are open to boys and girls, with separate groups. Dates are announced on QCDC's event calendar before each school holiday.
highlights: Separate groups for boys and girls
how_to_apply: Watch the QCDC event calendar before the summer and winter holidays
Register through the camp announcement
Attend all camp days
qcdc-career-camps.costs: Check each camp announcement for fees.

qcdc-career-development-workshop-series.about:
The Career Development Workshop Series is a QCDC initiative that helps participants acquire the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to manage their careers over the long term. Workshops focus on career exploration, IT-based career development skills and career planning at different stages, and complement QCDC's counselling (Al-Dileela), job-shadowing (My Career – My Future) and Career Village programmes.

Workshops are announced on QCDC's event calendar and social media; many are delivered in Arabic.
highlights: Run by Qatar Foundation's national career centre
qcdc-career-development-workshop-series.eligibility: Students and young people in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Follow the QCDC event calendar
Register for the workshop you want
Attend in person or online as announced

qcdc-career-village-2027.about:
Career Village is organised by QCDC with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, the Ministry of Labour and the Civil Service and Government Development Bureau. Over three days, organisations from government, energy, health, finance, media, security and other sectors run interactive stands and activities so students can experience different professions and understand the routes into them.

It is designed for secondary school students in Qatar's public and private schools (separate days for boys' and girls' public schools, other days for private schools and the public), as well as counsellors and parents. The seventh edition ran 28-30 September 2026 at KidZania Doha, Aspire Park; the next edition is expected in autumn 2027.

Attendance is free and usually arranged through schools.
highlights: Free for students, usually via school visits
qcdc-career-village-2027.eligibility: Secondary school students in Qatar (public and private schools), plus parents and counsellors.
how_to_apply: Ask your school career counsellor whether your school is registered
Check the QCDC event calendar in September
Attend on your school's allocated day or the public day

qcdc-little-employee.about:
Little Employee is QCDC's early career-awareness initiative. A parent or relative hosts the child at their workplace for a full day so the child can observe and help with real work, learn the value of work and start thinking about future careers and study choices. QCDC provides an introductory video and guidance for parents on what to expect.

The initiative is open worldwide to students aged 7 to 15 and is fully flexible: families pick any working day. It is a simple, free first step in career education for younger students.
highlights: Guidance materials for parents from QCDC
qcdc-little-employee.eligibility: Students aged 7-15 anywhere in the world, hosted by a parent or relative at their workplace.
how_to_apply: Read the Little Employee page and watch the intro video
Agree a day with the parent's employer
Spend the working day together and follow the QCDC guidance

qcdc-my-career-my-future-2027.about:
My Career – My Future is QCDC's flagship job-shadowing programme, run with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, the Ministry of Labour, the Ministry of Sports and Youth and the Civil Service and Government Development Bureau. Day 1 is an orientation at Multaqa, Education City; on days 2-4 students shadow professionals at a host organisation in their chosen field (medicine, aviation, energy, media, telecoms, finance, engineering, technology, judiciary, sport management, humanitarian work and more); day 5 is a closing ceremony with a university fair, competitions and certificates.

The 2026 edition was the largest so far and ran in early August, with registration closing in late July. QCDC also ran a Winter Edition in December 2025. The 2027 summer edition is expected to open for registration around June-July 2027.

It is the most structured way for a Qatar high school student to test a career before choosing a university major.
highlights: Three days inside a real workplace of your chosen field
qcdc-my-career-my-future-2027.eligibility: Arabic-speaking high school students in Qatar in grades 10, 11 and 12. Seats are limited per field.
how_to_apply: Watch the QCDC event calendar from June 2027
Complete the online registration form and pick a career field
Pay the registration fee using the instructions emailed to you
Attend the orientation at Multaqa, Education City
qcdc-my-career-my-future-2027.costs: Registration fee QAR 350 (2026), refundable if cancelled before the deadline.

qdb-lean-startup-program.about:
The Lean Startup Program, run by Qatar Development Bank through the Qatar Business Incubation Center (QBIC), supports sector-agnostic early-stage tech startups (sports tech, fashion tech, mobility, ICT, fintech and more). Benefits listed on the government's Startup Qatar portal include office space for one year to obtain a licence and register a company in Qatar, one year of bi-weekly coaching with a lean-certified business coach, marketing exposure and networking at QDB-sponsored events (including Web Summit), and investment of up to QAR 100,000.

Intake starts with a three-day QDB hackathon for idea-stage startups to build their business model and pitch deck; graduates pitch at a Mini Demo Day (usually early December) and can move on to the Lean Acceleration Program and its Demo Day in June.
highlights: One year of office space and coaching
Demo Day with QDB and angel investors
qdb-lean-startup-program.eligibility: Early-stage technology startups and founders in Qatar (age 18+).
how_to_apply: Read the programme on the Startup Qatar portal
Join the next QDB incubation hackathon / intake
Apply through QDB/QBIC and pitch to the selection committee
qdb-lean-startup-program.costs: Free; QDB invests up to QAR 100,000 in selected startups.

qf-ability-friendly-program.about:
The Ability Friendly Program (AFP), launched in 2018 within QF's Pre-University Education, offers tailored sports and developmental activities, such as specialised camps, football and swimming classes, for children and adults with special needs and disabilities. Registration is by email or phone.

The Qader Award lets community members join regardless of financial ability: recipients can enrol in accessible swimming or football programmes for an entire academic year at no cost. It is held annually, with online applications opening in March.
highlights: Swimming, football and camps adapted to each participant
Qader Award: a free year of classes
qf-ability-friendly-program.eligibility: Children and adults with special needs and disabilities in Qatar; Qader Award for families with financial need.
how_to_apply: Email abilityfriendly@qf.org.qa or call +974 4454 1398 to register
For the Qader Award, apply online when applications open in March
Attend the assessed class or camp
qf-ability-friendly-program.costs: Programme fees apply; the Qader Award covers a full academic year for selected applicants.

qf-ability-friendly-volunteering.about:
QF's Ability Friendly Program engages volunteers in its sports classes, camps and events for children and adults with disabilities. Volunteers aged 11 and above from Education City schools and universities, Qatar Foundation staff and community members are welcome to apply.

The programme also offers disability-awareness workshops and inclusion modules that teach how to support participants to access sport. It is a meaningful, hands-on volunteering option for school students building a service record.
highlights: Hands-on support at sports classes and events
qf-ability-friendly-volunteering.eligibility: Students aged 11+ from Education City schools and universities, QF staff and community members in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Email abilityfriendly@qf.org.qa to express interest
Complete any awareness training offered
Join classes and events as a volunteer

qf-akhlaquna-award-2027.about:
Akhlaquna is an initiative launched by Her Highness Sheikha Moza bint Nasser that highlights the link between knowledge and ethics. Its award recognises morally influential people with impactful initiatives inspired by values such as mercy, tolerance, honesty, generosity, humility, trustworthiness, justice and equality. Categories are Akhlaquna Junior (ages 7-14), Akhlaquna Youth (14-18), Individual Contributions (19-45, with a youth-led 'Al-Shabab' category added in 2026) and an Appreciation Award.

For the 2026 cycle, QF opened registration on 13 October 2025 and accepted entries until 11 January 2026. The 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same autumn-winter pattern; check the Akhlaquna website for the current call.
highlights: Junior and Youth categories for school students
qf-akhlaquna-award-2027.eligibility: Students and young people with an ethics-driven initiative; see the Akhlaquna site for residency rules of each category.
how_to_apply: Open akhlaquna.qa and check the current cycle
Choose the category matching your age
Describe your initiative and its impact in the online form
Submit before the deadline (January in the 2026 cycle)

qf-mehnaty-al-meydan-internships.about:
Qatar Foundation's internship platform connects students at QF partner universities (Carnegie Mellon, Georgetown, Northwestern, Texas A&M, VCUarts, Weill Cornell, HBKU and others in Education City) with QF entities. Mehnaty is a paid work-study programme (up to 20 hours a week during the semester at QAR 50 per hour, GPA 2.5+). Al Meydan is a structured unpaid internship (up to 20 hours a week in term and 40 in breaks, GPA 2.0+, juniors and sophomores prioritised).

Current postings include an Education City tour guide, an Oxygen Park event assistant and a data analyst intern at the Student Life Office, each with its own deadline. It is the easiest way for Education City students to gain paid campus experience.
highlights: Roles across all Qatar Foundation centres
qf-mehnaty-al-meydan-internships.eligibility: Students enrolled at a Qatar Foundation university in Education City (GPA 2.5+ for Mehnaty, 2.0+ for Al Meydan). Scholarship holders must check their scholarship allows work.
how_to_apply: Log in to internships.qf.org.qa
Browse current opportunities
Apply before each role's deadline
Interview with the host department
qf-mehnaty-al-meydan-internships.costs: Mehnaty pays QAR 50 per hour; Al Meydan is unpaid.

qlc-international-fellowship-program-202.about:
The International Fellowship Program is one of QLC's Young Leaders programmes. It develops international leadership, diplomatic and academic skills: fellows interact with global leaders, diplomats and experts, build professional networks and deepen their understanding of global citizenship and international governance during a summer programme in the United States of up to seven weeks, preceded by two preparatory modules in Doha.

The 2025 call (deadline 23 January 2025) targeted outstanding Qatari students, with eligibility listed as Qatari nationality, under 20 and in secondary school grades 10-12 with at least 85%, while the programme description refers to third- and fourth-year university students. Check the current call for the exact level. A new cycle is expected each winter with a January deadline.
highlights: Summer leadership programme in the USA
qlc-international-fellowship-program-202.eligibility: Qatari nationals; check the current call for level (secondary grades 10-12 under 20 with 85%+, or 3rd/4th-year university students).
how_to_apply: Watch the QLC Young Leaders pages from November
Register on the QLC portal
Upload ID, passport, transcript and a personal essay with parental consent
Complete assessments and interviews
qlc-international-fellowship-program-202.costs: Programme costs covered by QLC; a QAR 2,000 deposit applies to selected participants.

qlc-tomorrows-leaders-camp-2027.about:
Tomorrow's Leaders Camp is part of QLC's Young Leaders Program. It is an educational camp focused on community service and personal development: through practical projects students make a tangible community impact while building teamwork, effective communication, problem-solving, resilience, self-confidence and leadership traits. The programme mixes interactive activities and workshops, in Arabic and English, on weekday mornings in Doha.

The 2026 edition ran 5-16 July with a 10-day boys' camp and a 10-day girls' camp. Applicants must be Qatari, under 20, in grades 10-12 with at least 85% in their first-semester results; documents include ID, passport, transcript, a personal essay and parental consent, and selected students pay a QAR 2,000 refundable-on-completion deposit. The 2027 camp is expected on the same summer pattern.
highlights: Run by Qatar's national leadership centre
qlc-tomorrows-leaders-camp-2027.eligibility: Qatari nationals in grades 10-12, under 20, with 85%+ first-semester average.
how_to_apply: Register on the QLC portal when the 2027 call opens (spring)
Upload ID, passport, transcript, personal essay and parental consent
Pass the assessment stages
Submit a medical fitness certificate and the QAR 2,000 deposit if selected
qlc-tomorrows-leaders-camp-2027.costs: Free programme; QAR 2,000 security deposit (non-refundable if you withdraw or are absent).

qrdi-urep-undergraduate-research-experie.about:
UREP, now run by the QRDI Council (formerly QNRF), lets teams of undergraduate students work on research projects with faculty mentors at universities in Qatar, including Qatar University, UDST, Weill Cornell Medicine-Qatar, Texas A&M Qatar, Carnegie Mellon Qatar and Georgetown Qatar. Funded teams later present their results at the UREP competition; the 17th competition (November 2025) featured projects from a rehabilitation robot to drone systems for solar panels, judged on scientific merit, outcomes, learning and presentation, alongside the BRIO image award.

Proposals are submitted by faculty with their student teams; recent calls opened in mid-November and closed in mid-January. Students interested should approach a faculty member at their university about joining a UREP proposal.
highlights: National competition with oral and poster awards
Open to students at universities across Qatar
qrdi-urep-undergraduate-research-experie.eligibility: Full-time undergraduate students at universities in Qatar, applying with a faculty mentor.
how_to_apply: Talk to a faculty member about a UREP project
Prepare the proposal together with your team
Submit through the QRDI submission system during the call
Present results at the UREP competition
qrdi-urep-undergraduate-research-experie.costs: Funded by QRDI Council; free for students.

qsc-npc-data-summer-camp-2027.about:
The Data Summer Camp is organised by Qatar's National Planning Council (NPC) in partnership with the Qatar Scientific Club and with Microsoft Qatar. Over five days, students move from data basics and sources to processing and quality checks, learn about Qatar's National Data Programme, and design interactive dashboards with Power BI and AI tools. They finish by developing and presenting data-driven projects linked to Qatar National Vision 2030 (schools, population growth, healthcare access, traffic safety, tourism, utilities).

The second edition ran 8-12 August 2026 with about 40 students aged 14-17. A third edition is expected in summer 2027; announcements come through QSC and NPC channels.
highlights: Power BI and AI dashboards, taught with Microsoft Qatar
how_to_apply: Follow the Qatar Scientific Club for the 2027 announcement (around June-July)
Register through the QSC site
Attend all five days and present your project

qsc-science-workshops.about:
The Qatar Scientific Club, a youth body of the Ministry of Sports and Youth, runs a rolling calendar of short workshops. Current listings include 'Smart Agriculture and its Role in Sustainability', 'Sustainability and Waste Management' and 'Environment and Sustainability', each covering core concepts, technologies and future challenges, with a certificate of participation. Earlier workshops covered engineering for a sustainable environment, electronics and programming.

Registration is online, either as a participant or as a parent; acceptance is confirmed by email or SMS. Many workshops are free; paid ones (around QAR 100) are paid within 24 hours of acceptance. Workshops are usually in Arabic.
highlights: Topics from smart agriculture to electronics
qsc-science-workshops.eligibility: Young people in Qatar; age range set per workshop. Mostly Arabic.
how_to_apply: Open the QSC events page
Choose a workshop and register as participant or parent
Wait for the acceptance email/SMS
Pay within 24 hours if the workshop has a fee
qsc-science-workshops.costs: Many workshops free; some around QAR 100.

qsc-summer-science-camp-2027.about:
Every summer the Qatar Scientific Club runs a science camp to use the school holiday for building science, technology and innovation skills. The 2026 edition, 'Pioneers of Science and Technology', ran from 28 June to 20 August and included the fifth Future Engineer programme with the Public Works Authority (Ashghal), where 40 participants developed six projects (energy saving, worker protection, pothole detection, smart cities), and the second STEM summer programme with the Qatar Society of Engineers, a two-week course ending in projects such as solar villages and sea robots.

The camp is aimed at school and university-age young people in Qatar and is delivered mainly in Arabic. The 2027 edition is expected on the same summer pattern; registration is through the QSC website.
highlights: Engineering projects with Ashghal and the Qatar Society of Engineers
Weeks of hands-on workshops in QSC labs
Team projects presented at the end
qsc-summer-science-camp-2027.eligibility: Young people in Qatar (school and university age, by programme). Mainly in Arabic.
how_to_apply: Watch the QSC website and social media from May 2027
Register through the QSC site for the programme you want
Attend the workshops and present your team project
qsc-summer-science-camp-2027.costs: Most QSC programmes are free; some workshops charge a small fee.

qsc-volunteer-program.about:
The Qatar Scientific Club runs large science activities through the year, including its summer camp, the Young Inventors Programme and national robotics events, and accepts volunteers to help with organisation, labs and participants. Volunteers register through a bilingual online form (name, gender, date of birth, nationality and contact details) and are contacted when roles are available.

It is a practical way for students interested in science and engineering to gain volunteering hours and get to know Qatar's youth science community.
highlights: Help at science camps and competitions
Open to all nationalities in Qatar
qsc-volunteer-program.eligibility: Young people living in Qatar, any nationality.
how_to_apply: Open the QSC volunteer page
Fill in the online form
Wait to be contacted for upcoming events

qsc-young-inventors-program.about:
The Young Inventors Programme was launched by the Ministry of Sports and Youth at Web Summit Qatar 2026 and is run by the Qatar Scientific Club (QSC). Participants learn design thinking, engineering design and project execution, then work in teams through problem definition, idea generation, prototype design, testing and improvement, using QSC's labs and mentors.

The first cohort (35 young men and women) built seven prototypes, including a drone-detection device, a worker-safety monitoring system and a smart cast. The second cohort started on 13 September 2026 after remote interviews with applicants; new cohorts are announced on QSC's website and social media.

It suits young people who already have an invention idea and want hands-on engineering support in Arabic.
highlights: Access to QSC labs and engineering mentors
qsc-young-inventors-program.eligibility: Young Qatari men and women (programme run in Arabic). Applicants are interviewed remotely before acceptance.
how_to_apply: Follow QSC's website and social media for the next cohort call
Register on the QSC site
Attend the remote interview
Join the cohort and develop your prototype

qstp-ai-tinkerers-doha.about:
AI Tinkerers Doha is the local chapter of a global community of people who build with AI. QSTP hosts the sessions in Education City in partnership with Scale AI: each evening features project demos, hands-on learning and open discussion, and participants are encouraged to bring and present what they are working on.

Session 4 took place on 19 October 2026 at QSTP Tech2; new sessions are posted on QSTP's events page. It is an easy way for university students interested in AI to meet founders and engineers in Qatar.
highlights: Demo your AI project to a real builder community
qstp-ai-tinkerers-doha.eligibility: AI builders, developers, practitioners and students in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Check the QSTP events page for the next session
Register through the event link
Bring a project to demo (optional)

qstp-build-for-qstp-hackathons.about:
Build for QSTP is a recurring hackathon series hosted at Qatar Science & Technology Park in Education City. Each edition has its own theme and challenge brief (incubation, operations, internships, Stars of Science, sustainability, social impact and more), and teams of 2-4 developers, designers and business thinkers research, prototype and pitch within one or two days, with mentors on hand throughout.

Recent editions included the Incubation Hackathon (2-3 May 2026), Operations Hackathon (23-24 May 2026), Stars of Science Hackathon (11-14 June 2026) and an Internship Edition (30 July-2 August 2026) with cash prizes. Winning solutions can be piloted inside QSTP and first-place teams have been fast-tracked into QSTP's Entry Track.

It suits university students who want hands-on building experience and a route into Qatar's startup ecosystem. Upcoming themes are announced on the programme page and QSTP's social media.
highlights: Real challenges set by QSTP teams
Mentors, judges, cash prizes in some editions
Winners can be piloted or fast-tracked into QSTP programmes
qstp-build-for-qstp-hackathons.eligibility: University students, recent graduates and working professionals in Qatar. Teams of 2-4; you can form a team at the event.
how_to_apply: Check the Build for QSTP page for the next theme
Register through the event link
Form or join a team of 2-4
Build and pitch to the judges at QSTP

qstp-creative-labs.about:
Creative Labs is an intensive two-week studio programme at Qatar Science & Technology Park developed with NuVuX Studios. Participants join one of four parallel studios of 10-15 people (past studios: Health Wearables Devices, Games for Good, Aging in the City and more) and learn design-first principles, digital tools, 3D printing, laser cutting and prototyping by building a real project.

It is aimed at STEM educators and at school, undergraduate and graduate students interested in educational innovation and technology. The 2025 edition ran 10-21 August for 40-50 participants; QSTP currently collects registrations of interest for the next edition.

It is a rare chance in Doha to work MIT-style in a maker studio and leave with a finished prototype.
highlights: Studio method from NuVuX (MIT Labs heritage)
Hands-on prototyping with 3D printers and laser cutters
qstp-creative-labs.eligibility: STEM students (school, undergraduate, graduate) and STEM educators in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Open the Creative Labs page
Fill in the Register Your Interest form
Wait for QSTP to announce the next edition and confirm your place
qstp-creative-labs.costs: Not stated; contact QSTP for fees, if any.

qu-gateway-high-school-stem.about:
The Gateway to Qatar University (QU Gateway) programme, run by the Qatar University Young Scientists Center (an expansion of the Al-Bairaq programme founded in 2010), bridges school and university by giving national youth hands-on STEM experience. High school students work in STEM workshops and research activities with QU undergraduate mentors, faculty and QUYSC professionals.

Each cycle has 12-15 one-hour sessions for 20-25 students in grades 10-12, ending with a ceremony where students present orally or with posters and take part in science-filming, photography and video contests; winners receive awards and all get certificates. Separate cycles run for preparatory (middle) schools.
highlights: Mentored by QU faculty and students
Strong bridge into STEM majors at QU
qu-gateway-high-school-stem.eligibility: Students in grades 10-12 in Qatar (focus on national students), usually through their schools.
how_to_apply: Ask your school about participating in QU Gateway
Or contact the QU Young Scientists Center
Attend the sessions and present at the final ceremony

qu-i-am-a-researcher.about:
'I am a Researcher' (IR) gives pre-university students in Qatar advanced research experience in real labs at Qatar University's research institutions and departments. Nominated students work with professors and researchers, learn research methodology and manage hands-on projects; a recent online edition focused on game and mobile-app development using Java, C++, Python and Unity.

The track runs 2-3 months at 2-4 hours a week for grades 10-12, with 1-2 students per project. Participants receive certificates and volunteering letters, present at a final ceremony and can enter national and international competitions; the programme helped Qatar win its first ISEF award in 2019.
highlights: Pathway to ISEF and other competitions
qu-i-am-a-researcher.eligibility: Qatari high school students in grades 10-12, nominated through schools or QUYSC.
how_to_apply: Ask your school science coordinator about nomination
Or contact the QU Young Scientists Center
Work with your mentor 2-4 hours a week and present at the final ceremony

qu-national-science-promotion-program.about:
The National Science Promotion Program (NSPP), launched by the QU Young Scientists Center with the Office of the Vice President for Research and Graduate Studies, uses a 'learning by doing' approach. QU faculty submit STEM project proposals; each selected project hosts one QU undergraduate and two national high school students, who learn to form hypotheses, collect data, experiment and draw conclusions with professional lab equipment.

Students spend 2-4 hours a week for six months, finish with oral/poster presentations and contests, and receive certificates, volunteering letters and awards, plus opportunities to join national and international competitions. Recent projects range from functional foods for children with diabetes to materials science.
highlights: Real lab research at Qatar University
Route into national and international competitions
qu-national-science-promotion-program.eligibility: Qatari high school students (grades 10-12, with grade 12 the main focus).
how_to_apply: Contact the QU Young Scientists Center or your school coordinator
Get matched to a faculty-led project
Commit 2-4 hours a week for six months
